summary: This is the first run, so every event is treated as new. Several unrelated-looking incidents occurred in the last 5 days: the FAA nationwide ground stop on Nov 13 and its follow-ups, a United Airlines outage, a JPMorgan Chase glitch, an Apple outage and minor Cloudflare incidents. US stocks fell about 1% on Nov 17 and Bitcoin is down about 13% on the week, but no exchange halts or outages turned up. No official source reports a cyber attack, and stated causes differ by event. Several causes are still unknown, and I did not check telecom or geopolitical sources in depth this run.

events.title: FAA nationwide ground stop after telecom/router failure, with follow-on actions
events.impact: Departures halted nationwide for 4+ hours (start time approximate), tens of thousands of flights affected. On Nov 17 the FAA paused installing new routers. Event predates the 72h window; kept for context.
events.stated_cause: Officials say a Juniper router installed in Arkansas overloaded older systems. Root cause not yet determined. DHS and officials say no indication of malicious activity. Accounts differ somewhat: equipment failure vs new tech added to old system.

events.title: United Airlines systemwide technology outage
events.impact: Departing flights affected Monday afternoon (exact time not seen); United later said the issue was resolved.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Only reported as a technology issue; no link to the FAA incident has been stated.

events.title: JPMorgan Chase technical issue affecting transactions
events.impact: Customer transactions disrupted; Chase said transactions resumed around 11:49 GMT Nov 17. Start time approximate. Reports of other banks being down were not verified.
events.stated_cause: Unknown; described only as a technical issue. A live blog asked whether it was tied to last week's Microsoft and air traffic disruptions; I saw only a one-word answer, no.

events.title: US stocks fall; S&P 500 lowest close since late July
events.impact: Checked against price data: Dow -1.64% to 50,759, S&P 500 -1.03% to 7,340.53, Nasdaq -0.74%, VIX up about 11% to about 25.5. A broad but orderly decline; no halts or exchange glitches seen.
events.stated_cause: Market reports cite chip-stock selling before Nvidia earnings and rate-hike worries after hot CPI data. Nvidia rose after hours on its results.

events.title: Bitcoin about 13% lower over 7 days, trading near 64-65K USD
events.impact: Price data (Coinbase, CoinGecko, Fortune) shows BTC around 64-65K, roughly -13% on the week but only about +/-2% over 24h. This does not match a viral 'crypto crashing now' claim; it is a gradual weekly drop. No exchange outage found.
events.stated_cause: Not stated in the sources checked; unknown.

events.title: Apple services (iCloud, Apple Pay, App Store, Music) outage
events.impact: Multiple Apple services listed as down on Apple's status page per a live blog; most recovered by about 20:34 UTC, with AppleCare on Device the last one listed.
events.stated_cause: Unknown; no cause seen in sources.

events.title: Cloudflare minor incidents (Durable Objects, LAX, Ashburn); status shows degraded
events.impact: Official feed shows Sites and Services at degraded performance as of 03:39 UTC. Third-party trackers list Durable Objects timeouts plus regional network issues. Cloudflare logs dozens of such incidents a month, so this is near base rate.
events.stated_cause: Elevated timeouts on Durable Objects and regional network performance issues; no deeper cause published yet.

events.title: CISA adds actively exploited flaws to KEV (Cisco BroadWorks, Barracuda, Outlook, Chrome, Check Point)
events.impact: Routine but active exploitation: six flaws added Nov 10, two more (Check Point Gaia, UnrealIRCd) on Nov 13. A researcher report links the BroadWorks flaw to attacks on a European telecom provider. I saw no new CISA Emergency Directive in this window.
events.stated_cause: Active exploitation of vendor vulnerabilities; patching deadlines of Nov 16 and Nov 24 for federal agencies.

events.title: AWS Middle East regions (UAE me-central-1, Bahrain me-south-1) long-running disruption
events.impact: AWS says data in Bahrain and one UAE zone cannot be restored; most customers moved to other regions. Latest feed updates are dated Sep 15. Start month is March; exact day not in feed.
events.stated_cause: AWS describes infrastructure damage across multiple zones; the feed does not give a cause beyond that. Cause beyond that: unknown.

events.title: Viral claim of a nationwide 90-day blackout on Nov 17
events.impact: No outage found. Reporting says there was no federal announcement; a FEMA test alert was scheduled.
events.stated_cause: Social media rumor; no official source supports it.

connection_assessment.reasoning: No shared vendor, official common cause or common failure signature found. The FAA event has a stated router/telecom cause. The market move is attributed to Nvidia/inflation worries. Causes for United, Chase, Apple and Cloudflare are unknown. Windows partly overlap (Nov 13-17), but that alone is weak evidence.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official or vendor statement naming a shared provider or attacker, the same failure signature across United, Chase, Apple and FAA, exchange halts or payment-network failures, or a new CISA Emergency Directive tied to these systems.

alert.reason: Level is yellow; no official attribution to an attack and no evidence of linkage or of ongoing critical-system failure.

prep_note: If you travel, check your airline app before leaving, since FAA and airline systems are still recovering. Keep a backup payment method and some cash in case bank or card apps glitch. Apply pending patches for Cisco, Check Point, Barracuda, Chrome and Outlook if you run them. Watch for FAA, CISA or wire-service updates on the router root cause.
